sprints.title: The core: runtime keys, thread-bound entries, async startup factories

tasks.title: Service keys that are not Rust types
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Introduce `ServiceKey` (`Type(TypeId)` / `Runtime(RuntimeKey)`) in `rayx_core::di` and key the registry's descriptors, caches, resolution guards and scope caches by it (d-runtime-keys). Add `RuntimeKey::new(name)`, keyed registration (`add_singleton_keyed`, `add_scoped_keyed`, `add_transient_keyed`, factories returning an erased `Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>` or a resolution error) and keyed resolution (`service_by_key`, `required_service_by_key`). The typed API keeps its signatures and behavior. New group `crates/rayx_core/tests/di_runtime_keys.rs`: each lifetime by key, scopes sharing singletons, a factory resolving typed and keyed services, a missing key (optional and required, the error naming it), two keys of the same name staying distinct.

tasks.title: Services kept on the thread that made them
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add thread-bound registration, typed and keyed, for values that are neither `Send` nor `Sync` (d-thread-bound): a `Send + Sync` slot in the provider, the value in a `thread_local!` table of its thread, `ServiceResolutionError::WrongThread` elsewhere, an orphan list drained by the owning thread for slots dropped elsewhere. No `unsafe`. New group `crates/rayx_core/tests/di_thread_bound.rs`: resolve on the owning thread (each lifetime), resolve from another thread (error, value untouched), drop the provider on another thread (the value's drop runs later on its own thread, observed with an `Rc` drop counter), typed services of the same provider usable from both threads. `c-core-wasm` proves the wasm32 build.

tasks.title: Runtime-keyed startup services with async factories
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Give `StartupServiceType` the two key kinds (name as `Cow<'static, str>`) and `StartupRegistry` asynchronous factories (`add_resolved_async`); the run resolves every startup service (awaiting async factories) before ordering and initializing (d-startup-async). New group `crates/rayx_core/tests/di_startup_runtime.rs`: an async-made runtime-keyed service initialized in the run; ordering runtime → type and type → runtime; a layer initialized concurrently; its timeout and the default; a failing initialize, a failing factory and a timeout each reported with the display name; the run fails unless all initialized.

tasks.title: `startup_service_type` keyed by registration
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Make `StartupInitializable::startup_service_type` a provided method (`None` by default) and key a startup service by the explicit type, else by its registration key (d-startup-async); update the `add_startup_*` extension methods to record it and `docs/startup.md`'s Rust example to leave the method out. New group `crates/rayx_core/tests/di_startup_registration_key.rs`: `add_startup_singleton::<T>`, `add_startup_singleton_as::<dyn X>`, scoped and transient forms keyed by registration; a dependency on that key waits; an explicit implementation keeps its key; `StartupRegistry::add` keys by the concrete type.

sprints.title: The TS builder, provider and start, Rust's start, the Rust names

tasks.title: TS `ServiceProvider` with class tokens
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Add `#[class] ServiceProvider` in `rayx_app::ts` (d-provider): `getService`, `getRequiredService`, `createScope`, `dispose`, view models activated until disposal; token arguments as `JsHandle`s, RayX's service classes recognized by `JsHandle::constructor()` and keyed by `Constructor`; typed declarations over `ServiceKey<T>` (d-ts-signatures); the static resolver table for RayX's service classes (one wrapper object per resolved `Arc` per provider); the surface's token table for runtime keys (used by s3). Rust bridges take `Instance<ServiceProvider>`. `AppServices` and `ServiceScope` stay until t11 removes them. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_provider.rs` (a headless TSX app as `nsh_tsx_services.rs` runs one): resolve by class, `===` for a singleton, `null` and the thrown error for a missing token, a scope's scoped service, `dispose` releasing it and deactivating a view model, use after dispose throwing, the declarations typing `getService` and `getRequiredService`.

**Implementation notes (against `nshx-0.5.0-4`):** a resolved RayX service is a class *instance* made in Rust, which cannot become a `JsHandle` without the JS host, so lookups return a `Resolved` (an `nsh_core::element::Ret` that gives the instance's object, a kept `JsHandle` or `null`), and the token parameter is a `ServiceKeyArg` (`Arg`: the `JsHandle` plus a name for messages); both are declared by the typed `#[ts]` signatures. The wrapper cache keeps one `Instance` per resolved `Arc` per provider. Synchronous class members cannot reach `global`, so the surface's token table and the root's one TS object live in VM `Local`s (`sys.locals`). `ServiceKey<T>` names `ServiceToken<T>`, so a minimal generic `ServiceToken` (name only) is added here; t13 adds the registrations. `rayx_app::ts::register(registry)` registers every TS class and the alias (t12 builds `rayx_app::register` on it).

tasks.title: TS `RayXAppBuilder` with every builder method
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add `#[class] RayXAppBuilder` (d-ts-builder): `new` starts from `add_nsh_services()`; each chaining member delegates to the Rust extension method of the same name (the list in BLD-1), `defaultInitializationTimeout` in milliseconds, `configureAppConfiguration` with a recording configuration builder. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_builder.rs`: a TSX app built with each method resolves each service through the provider (t06), implied dependencies present, the declarations declaring each method, `Registry::undocumented` empty. Options callbacks come in t08.

tasks.title: Options callbacks from TS
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add the recording options classes (`I18nOptions`, `NavigationOptions`, `AssetOptions`, `FontOptions`, `InputMapOptions`) with Rust's configure methods in camelCase, called during the builder call; replay the recorded patch in the Rust `configure` closure (d-ts-builder). New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_builder_options.rs`: a value from the callback overrides `appsettings.json`'s, one it leaves alone keeps the bound value, each options class reaches its service, a throwing callback throws at the builder call with its message.

tasks.title: `await builder.start()`
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Generalize the surface startup to take a builder (`start_app_with`, d-start) and add the async member `start` resolving with the root `ServiceProvider`, then keeping the platform and suspension services current. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_start.rs`: success, rejection for a failing service, a timeout, an option validated on start and a failing ready hook (each with the startup error's message), a second `start` resolving with the same root, the platform snapshot following NSH's environment afterwards, two engines building two providers.

tasks.title: Rust's start without `set_app`
tasks.descriptionMarkdown:
Add the extension trait giving `RayXAppBuilder::start()` and `start_async()` (d-start); remove `set_app`, the global builder function, `AppError::NoApp` and `rayx_app::start()`/`start_app()`; reword `AppError`'s messages. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_app_start.rs`: a Rust root's `app_state()` moving through its states, `start_async` returning the root or the error, a second start keeping the first root, two surfaces with two providers.

**Implementation note:** a Rust root's chain runs before `start()` adds NSH's services, so `add_storage()` would have registered the in-memory store first. `rayx_runtime`'s `add_storage()` now makes the platform's `PlatformKeyValueStore` (which `add_nsh_services` registers) the app's store when there is one, in either order, as the asset reader and suspension host are already resolved lazily; `start_app_with` adds NSH's services where the app registered none. New `AppError::BuilderStarted` for a TS builder used after `start()`.

tasks.title: Rust names for the TS service classes; the old API removed
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Rename the TS service classes to the Rust services' names in `rayx_app::ts` (RES-2's list), drop their `of(app)` statics, make `NavigationRegion` from `navigationService.region(name)`, remove `AppServices` and `ServiceScope` (d-provider); update `rayx_app`'s and the umbrella's exports and prelude. Move every existing `rayx_app` test group and `crates/rayx/tests/umbrella.rs` from `set_app` / `AppServices` / `X.of(app)` to the builder, provider and new names. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_class_names.rs`: the set's declarations name each new class and none of the old ones. `c-app-groups` runs the crate's groups (reason in its description).

sprints.title: One-line crates, extensions, and services written in TypeScript

tasks.title: TS services in the container
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add `addSingleton` / `addScoped` / `addTransient` and their `As` forms with `ServiceToken<T>` (d-ts-services): thread-bound runtime-keyed entries holding `JsHandle`s, typed over `ServiceKey<T>` with a generic `ServiceToken<T>` (d-ts-signatures), factories as callbacks (`call` from a TS resolve, `call_async` from the startup run), contract and startup singletons made during `start()`. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_container.rs`: each lifetime's identity (`===`), a factory resolving Rust and TS services, `As` under a `ServiceToken`, a scope releasing its TS services, a Rust thread resolving a TS service getting the wrong-thread error, Rust resolving a not-yet-made TS service outside a JS call getting its error, the declarations typing each registration and `ServiceToken<T>`.

tasks.title: TS `AsyncInitializable` and `StartupInitializable`
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Declare the two interfaces through NSH's `#[interface]` with `async fn` members and the agreed TS shapes, `StartupInitializable` repeating `AsyncInitializable`'s members (d-ts-startup, d-ts-signatures), add `StartupInitializationState` and `StartupInitializationContext`, the `addStartup*` registrations and the Rust stand-in in the startup run (d-ts-startup). New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_startup.rs`: the declarations; `initialize` awaited once and skipped when `isInitialized()`, asked just before initializing, is true; `startupServiceType`, `initializationDependsOn` and `initializationTimeout` read once; TS → Rust and Rust → TS (via a contract from t16, or a `ServiceToken` dependency) ordering; `initializationTimeout` in ms and the default; failure by throw, rejection and timeout naming the TS class; the registration token as key.

tasks.title: TS ready hooks
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add `onReady` and `onReadyWhen` to the TS builder, adding `Callback`s to the same `ReadyHooks` list with a TS `ReadyContext` (d-ts-startup). New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_ready.rs`: TS and Rust hooks (one from an `apply`'d extension) in added order, a predicate that holds and one that does not, a throwing and a rejecting hook failing `start()`.

tasks.title: `#[rayx::contract]`
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add the attribute in `rayx_app_macros` (d-contracts): the `dyn`-compatible public trait, the hidden NSH `#[interface]` trait and its `Js<Trait>` stand-in, the token (its form and name brought to the owner first: it cannot carry the trait's name, d-contracts), the `Send + Sync` adapter over a thread-bound slot, registration `As` `dyn Trait` from TS; compile errors for generics, supertraits and methods returning a plain value. New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_contracts.rs`: Rust awaiting a TS method's result and error through `Arc<dyn Trait>`, a `()` method posted in order, a call off the engine thread getting `ContractError::WrongThread`, a Rust startup service depending on the contract initialized after the TS implementation.

tasks.title: TS options
tasks.descriptionMarkdown: Add a generic `OptionsToken<T>` with a typed `getOptions<T>` (d-ts-signatures), `addOptions` (bind, configure, validate, validateOnStart), `configureOptions` and `getOptions` (d-ts-options). New group `crates/rayx_app/tests/nsh_tsx_options.rs`: defaults, a bound section, configure callbacks in order, a failed validation on resolve, `validateOnStart` failing `start()` with its message.
